transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Big developments today in the tech world.
Ship giant NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang, Wall Street rallied,
and Megaspeed, the company associated with a suspected Chinese spy
entangled with Huang, is now on a Commerce Department blacklist.
Here's NPR's Shannon Bond.
The Commerce Department is adding Megaspeed to a list of companies
barred from buying advanced technology without a U.S. government license.
The Justice Department has said it's conducting a criminal investigation
into allegations Megaspeed has enabled China
to illegally access NVIDIA's most advanced chips.
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigned earlier this month
after reports he had an affair with a Megaspeed executive
who U.S. officials suspect was working with Chinese intelligence.
This week, NVIDIA's board reversed course and reinstated Huang.
Megaspeed didn't respond to a request for comment.
It previously denied wrongdoing and said the executive left the company last year.
Shannon Bond, NPR News.
The Federal Appeals Court has cleared the way for the Army
to detonate lead-based explosives at an Iowa facility.
The Army says the detonation will happen Wednesday morning,
but the status of the plan is not clear.
Iowa Public Radio's Grant Gerlock reports.
President Donald Trump said the detonation was on pause
until the Eighth Circuit ruled in favor of the operation.
Now the court says it can go forward.
The controlled explosion of nearly five tons of lead azide
at the Iowa Army ammunition plant has raised alarm
because it will create a drifting cloud of lead dust.
The judge's ruling says the EPA has taken necessary steps
to minimize the spread.
Preparations include sand barriers stacked two stories high
around the stored explosives.
Trump also says incoming Democratic governor Rob Sand
must approve the operation.
Sand says the administration should decide based on information
from experts on the ground.
For NPR News, I'm Grant Gerlock.
On social media, President Trump said he would blame sand
for any and all death or destruction
if the bomb-making material explodes spontaneously.
Sand, however, does not take office until January.
Brazil's former president has been in the hospital
since last Friday when he was transferred from house arrest.
Jair Bolsonaro serving a 27-year prison sentence
over an attempted coup.
Julia Canaro reports from Rio de Janeiro.
Jair Bolsonaro was diagnosed with acute bowel obstruction
and pneumonia and remains under intensive care
at a private hospital in Brasilia.
According to the latest medical report,
he is clinically stable, but there is no scheduled date
for his discharge, and further surgery remains a possibility
if his condition deteriorates.
His bowel condition is linked to the stab he suffered
in 2018 in a campaign rally before being elected president,
which has led to several surgeries.
This week marks a year since Bolsonaro started his 27-year sentence
for attempting a coup to stay in power after losing re-elections.
Since March, he has been under house arrest
due to his health conditions.
For NPR News, I'm Julia Canaro in Rio.
This is NPR.
Google made ways when the company refused to give schools
the option to turn AIO review off in search.
Now its own employees are weighing in.
Here's NPR's Sequoia Carillo.
J.A. Bolsonaro was diagnosed with acute bowel--
More than 550 Google employees signed a petition Friday
to allow schools access to search without AIO review.
In the petition, the union warns against trying to force schools
to adopt AIO, wearing that the all-or-nothing attitude
will drive teachers and students away from Google products altogether.
They say the rollout makes Google look like it is punishing schools
for not using AIO and could damage the reputation of the company.
Even though the petition is only supported
by a small percentage of Google employees,
the fear is not unfounded.
Since the company announced its policy on AIO review for schools,
protests have happened in six cities outside Google offices.
Sequoia Carillo, NPR News.
California Democratic Congressman Jimmy Gomez
resigning from Congress after the House Ethics Committee
released a report saying it found substantial evidence
that Gomez engaged in sexual misconduct toward a staffer.
Gomez says he has strong disagreements with the ethics panel's findings
but says he will resign on December 1st.
He was already set to leave Congress,
defeated in his bid for reelection by a fellow Democrat.
Cincinnati Zoo Hippo Co., back open to visitors,
had been closed following the death of the beloved hippo Fiona.
Zoo officials say new protective measures now in place
after Fiona swallowed a knit hat that was thrown by a visitor.
it got caught in a ceiling fan and ended up in the hippo habitat.
